And as mentioned at the time: "I can't imagine Iran accepting these conditions without any give, that especially with the renewed conflict with the US again.

As a reminder, the US naval blockade is back in force after the ceasefire deal fell apart.

And in case it needs reminding once again, control over the Strait of Hormuz remains Iran's biggest leverage over the US in the whole conflict.

It is literally their ace in the hole in being able to keep things going for this long and also in case nuclear talks hit a snag at some point in the future." That is not to say that Iran might not agree to some soft reopening of conditions along the strait as they did during the ceasefire deal.

But if one is expecting Iran to voluntarily give up control of the strait and to allow ship traffic to pick up significantly, that simply will not take place.
